notes: §1985:VII.3.9.2: VALUE OF {implementor-name-1 IS {data-name-1 | literal-1}} ..., the grammar's valueOfClause/valueOfEntry, and literal-1 is a 1985 literal: "Every literal belongs to one of two types: nonnumeric or numeric" (§1985:IV.4.2.2.2). kb/Work PB5416 (fixed): the national (N"...", NX"...") and boolean (B"...", BX"...") literals were gated at 85 only as a procedure-division statement operand (the version pass's statement-scoped arm), so VALUE OF ID IS N"AB", B"1" and NX"0041" compiled and ran FS=00 while VALUE OF ID IS X"4142" drew COBOL0900 from the literal token's screen. The national and boolean gates are now that same token screen's (LiteralScreen.GateFormat), position-blind, so each is COBOL0900 at 85 here as in a MOVE (witnesses: both pb5416 cases, two literals each). A numeric literal of more than 18 digits is implementor latitude in 1985 (§1985:IV.4.2.2.2.2 sets 18 as the least an implementor must allow), not a nonconformity of this rule; that the compiler's own 18-digit literal limit at 85 is asked only of procedure-division literals is a consistency point outside this rule. The legal side is 1985-FMT-VII_3_9_2.
